title: Capital Gain vs. Loss
takeaway: Selling silver can result in a capital gain or loss, which impacts your tax liability.

data.label: Capital Gain
data.evidence: Once you have your 1099-B and your records of the cost of your silver, you can calculate your capital gain or loss. This is done by subtracting the cost of the silver (Box 6 on the 1099-B) from the sales price (Box 2 on the 1099-B).

data.label: Capital Loss
data.evidence: If the sales price is lower than the cost, you have a capital loss, which can be used to offset other capital gains.

narration: The sale of silver coins is generally treated as a capital gain or loss. This calculation depends on the difference between the sales price and the original cost of the coins. Understanding this difference is crucial for accurate tax reporting.
